name: Piper PA-28 Cherokee / Warrior / Archer / Arrow
variants: Arrow (PA-28R, retractable; Arrow IV has a T-tail)
summary: Low-wing four-seat single family that rivals the Cessna 172 as the most common US trainer and private aircraft.

wings: Constant-chord 'Hershey bar' wing on early models; tapered outer panels on Warrior, Archer and later Arrows
engines: Single flat-four in a squared-off cowl with two air inlets either side of the spinner
fuselage: Four-seat cabin with a single door on the right side, over the wing
Fixed tricycle gear with oleo struts and wheel fairings (Arrow retracts)
Three side windows per side on later models
tail: Arrow IV variant has a T-tail

tellTales: Low-wing four-seater with fixed tricycle gear and a slim swept fin
One cabin door only, on the right side

confusedWith.howToTell: The Grumman has a sliding canopy and skinny tubular main gear legs; the PA-28 has a car-style right door and oleo-strut gear.
The Mooney has retractable gear and a vertical tail that appears swept forward; the PA-28 has a conventionally swept fin.
The PA-32 is longer with an extra side window and a double rear door on the left; the PA-28 has a shorter cabin and one door.
The PA-28 is a low-wing with no struts; the 172 is a strut-braced high-wing.
